_comment: Source of truth for the wiki: page order, the sidebar, prev/next paging, the search index
and public/sitemap.xml are all generated from this file by scripts/build-wiki.mjs.
Order here is reading order. Every .md under wiki/ must be listed, and every slug becomes
the URL /wiki/<slug>/ — changing a slug breaks inbound links, so treat them as permanent.
extraSitemap holds the non-wiki URLs the sitemap must still advertise.

hub.title: Open Historia Wiki
hub.description: How to install, play and master Open Historia — the free, open-source, AI-driven grand strategy game.

pages.title: Installing Open Historia
pages.description: Download and install on Windows, macOS, Linux and Android, or play straight away in your browser.

pages.title: Connecting an AI Provider
pages.description: Open Historia is driven by a language model you supply. Set up Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local model on your own machine.

pages.title: How to Play
pages.description: The core loop: pick a country, write orders in plain English, skip time, and read what the world did in response.

pages.title: Your First Campaign
pages.description: A guided first hour — from the main menu to your first war, told step by step.

pages.title: Starting a Game
pages.description: Scenarios, choosing a country, inventing your own faction, and what the six difficulty levels actually change.

pages.title: The Interface
pages.description: Every panel, button and badge on screen, and what each one is for.

pages.title: The World Map
pages.description: Reading the map: political fills, striped disputes, labels, the 3D globe, terrain and basemaps.

pages.title: Time and Turns
pages.description: Nothing happens until you skip time. Jump lengths, auto-jump, segmented skips and undoing a turn.

pages.title: Giving Orders
pages.description: The actions queue: writing orders in plain English, refining them, and how they get resolved.

pages.title: Events and History
pages.description: How a turn's events are revealed, categorised, remembered and eventually compacted.

pages.title: Diplomacy
pages.description: Talking to other countries: leader voices, group threads, memory, reactions and unprompted approaches.

pages.title: Relations, Treaties and War
pages.description: The four ledgers that decide who is at war with whom, how much they like each other, and what they have signed.

pages.title: Territory: Control, Sovereignty and Claims
pages.description: Who holds the ground, who lawfully owns it, and who says it is theirs — three separate layers, drawn differently.

pages.title: Military and Combat
pages.description: Unit types, strength, postures, movement ranges and the combat maths — plus the two switchable unit systems.

pages.title: Espionage
pages.description: Intelligence ratings, sending agents, being spied on, double agents and sealed intercepts.

pages.title: Projects and Operations
pages.description: Long-running efforts that span turns: research programmes, construction, covert operations and campaigns.

pages.title: National Statistics
pages.description: The stat sheet: strategic indices, population, GDP and the rest — where the numbers come from and how to track them.

pages.title: Countries and Identity
pages.description: Names, aliases, tags, flags, colours, reputation, leaders, and countries that hold no land at all.

pages.title: Cities and Structures
pages.description: Cities on the map and the bases, ports and landmarks that get built during a campaign.

pages.title: The Advisor
pages.description: Your in-game analyst: asking questions, reading charts, and turning advice into orders and projects.

pages.title: Settings Reference
pages.description: Every option in the game, what it does, and which ones are worth changing first.

pages.title: Cheats and the Game Master Console
pages.description: Twelve tools for rewriting the world by hand — annex territory, edit countries, author events, roll back turns.

pages.title: Saves, Rollback and Sharing
pages.description: How campaigns are stored, how to undo, how to clone, and how to move a game or scenario between machines.

pages.title: The Map Editor
pages.description: Draw your own world: regions, owners, cities, flags, basemaps and imported maps.

pages.title: The Community Hub
pages.description: Download scenarios other players have made, and publish your own.

pages.title: Hosting a Server
pages.description: Run Open Historia on your own machine, play offline, or reach it from your phone on the same network.

pages.title: Playing on Your Phone
pages.description: The Android app, what it downloads on first launch, and how it connects.

pages.title: AI Providers and Models
pages.description: Which providers work, which models to pick, what it costs, and the expert controls.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Blank maps, greyed-out AI, slow turns, CORS errors and the other things that go wrong.
